api_example.curl:
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/images/edits -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -F model="gpt-image-1.5" -F "image[]=@angle-1.png" -F prompt="$(cat prompt.txt)" -F quality="high" -F size="1536x1024"  # angle 1 first, prompt only — its finished result is the reference for the rest
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/images/edits -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -F model="gpt-image-1.5" -F "image[]=@angle-1-finished.png" -F "image[]=@angle-2.png" -F prompt="Image 1 is the finished look from this same space — match it exactly. $(cat prompt.txt)" -F quality="high" -F size="1536x1024"  # angles 2+: finished angle 1 first, raw angle second
api_example.note: ChatGPT UI is $0 extra if you already have ChatGPT. The API is pay-per-image — test on one batch first. Endpoint and model names change; verify at run time.

batch_inputs.api: POST /v1/images/edits — one call per angle. Angle 1: one image (the raw angle) with the recipe prompt only. Angles 2+: two images — image[0] = the finished angle 1, image[1] = the raw angle — with the chain line 'Image 1 is the finished look from this same space — match it exactly.' in front of the recipe prompt. Up to 16 images total per call. Model names change often — gpt-image-1 was shut down 2026-10-23; use the current gpt-image-1.5 / gpt-image-2.5 model at run time. Quality: high. Input fidelity: high where the model offers it.
batch_inputs.chatgpt_ui: Upload the 2-4 angles of the same space in one message with the recipe prompt. Angle 1 is edited first with the prompt only; then, for each remaining angle, send the finished angle 1 first and the raw angle second, with the chain line 'Image 1 is the finished look from this same space — match it exactly.' in front of the prompt. Do not start a new chat per angle.
batch_inputs.output_size: Match the input angle's aspect ratio. Do not let the model crop to square unless the input was square.

batch_workflow: 1. Shoot, then Auto HDR. Do not start AI edits on un-HDR'd originals.
2. Triage: pick the spaces that need extra — usually 1 exterior/yard set and 1-2 interior rooms. Pick which angle goes first for each space — that first photo sets the look for the rest.
3. Pick the recipe. Do not write a fresh prompt. Copy the recipe prompt exactly.

4. Batch: upload 2-4 angles of the SAME space, in the SAME message/call, with the recipe prompt pasted once. Angle 1 is edited first with the prompt only; its finished result is then the reference each remaining angle is matched to (finished angle 1 + raw angle, with the chain line 'Image 1 is the finished look from this same space — match it exactly.' in front of the prompt).

5. Review the whole set together, side by side. Check the QC list in the recipe. If one angle is off, fix ONLY that angle, with the finished first photo + the approved angles attached, and the full KEEP list repeated.
6. Approve, then save the approved set — it is the reference for any angle you add later. Name files with -Virtually-Staged / -Virtually-Landscaped, keep originals untouched.

7. Push to gallery: MLS-ready export (2048px long edge, sRGB, under 2 MB), add Matterport / Kuula / video links as iframe fields, deliver with text + email, follow up, ask for a review. See DELIVERY-CHECKLIST in RECIPE-PACK.md.

golden_rules: Never edit one angle alone. Always run all angles of that space together, in one batch, in one run — angle 1 first, the rest matched to it.

First photo sets the look. Angle 1 is edited first with the recipe prompt only, and its finished result is the reference the rest are matched to. Every other angle must match that finished first photo, not invent its own look.
KEEP list repeated every time. Say what must not change, in every prompt, every round. Drift builds up if you only say it once.
CHANGE ONLY list. Name exactly what may change. Everything else is frozen.
Materials are a closed list. Same lawn, same plants, same sofa, same table — exact items, exact colours. No synonyms, no 'similar'.
One change per round. If a result is close but one thing is wrong, fix only that one thing, and repeat the full KEEP list.
Never overwrite an original. Auto HDR originals stay untouched. Edited files get a new name with -Virtually-Staged or -Virtually-Landscaped.
Keep the approved set as the reference. The next angle you add later must match the approved set, not the first draft.

qc_checklist: House shape, roof, porch, door, and driveway identical to the real photo?
Is the lawn at least 80% of the yard — clean and open, not covered in beds?
Count the plantings: 5 or fewer total? Only hydrangeas, 1 red maple, 2 grasses?
Only ONE thin foundation bed — no foreground bed, no driveway bed, no rocks everywhere?
Trees still autumn, sky still blue, lighting still late-morning?
Does it look calm and simple like Jason's, not busy?
